The '''2011–12 Bundesliga''' was the 49th season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier [[Association football|football]] league. The season started on 5 August 2011 with the opening match involving defending champions [[Borussia Dortmund]] and ended with the last games on 5 May 2012. The traditional winter break was held between the weekends around 17 December 2011 and 20 January 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=Der Rahmenterminkalender 2011/12|trans-title=The Preliminary Calendar 2011/12|language=de|date=26 November 2010|access-date=29 March 2011|magazine=[[Kicker (sports magazine)|Kicker]]|location=Germany|url=https://www.kicker.de/der-rahmenterminkalender-20112f12-545423/artikel}}</ref>

The league comprised eighteen teams: The best fifteen teams of the [[2010–11 Bundesliga|2010–11 season]], the best two teams from the [[2010–11 2. Bundesliga]], and the winners of the [[2010–11 Bundesliga#Relegation play-offs|relegation play-off]] between the 16th-placed Bundesliga team and the third-placed 2. Bundesliga team.

Since Germany climbed from fourth to third place in the [[UEFA coefficient#League coefficient|UEFA association coefficient rankings]] at the end of the 2010–11 season,<ref>{{cite web|title=UEFA Country Ranking 2011|url=http://www.xs4all.nl/~kassiesa/bert/uefa/data/method4/crank2011.html|publisher=Bert Kassies|access-date=14 April 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Coefficient clamor – DW – 02/28/2011 |url=https://www.dw.com/en/bundesliga-secures-holy-grail-fourth-champions-league-place/a-14879816 |access-date=2023-06-05 |website=dw.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Honigstein |first=Raphael |date=2011-03-02 |title=Raphael Honigstein: Differing mindsets have Germany, Italy going in opposite directions |url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2011/03/02/bundesliga-serie |access-date=2023-06-05 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref> the league gained an additional group stage berth for the [[UEFA Champions League]].

==Teams==
The league comprised eighteen teams: [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] and [[FC St. Pauli]] were directly relegated after finishing the [[2010–11 Bundesliga|2010–11 season]] in the bottom two places. Frankfurt ended a six-year tenure in the Bundesliga, while St. Pauli only made a cameo one-year appearance in the top flight and directly returned to the second level.

The relegated teams were replaced by [[Hertha BSC]], champions of the [[2010–11 2. Bundesliga]], and runners-up [[FC Augsburg]]. The Bavarian side made their debut at the highest level of football in Germany, while Hertha directly returned to the Bundesliga after just one year at the second tier.

A further place in the league was decided through a two-legged play-off between [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], the 16th-placed team of the 2010–11 Bundesliga, and [[VfL Bochum]], the third-placed 2. Bundesliga team. Mönchengladbach won the series 2–1 on aggregate and therefore retained its Bundesliga spot.

===Stadiums and locations===
The most prominent change regarding stadiums occurred at Mainz, where [[FSV Mainz 05]] moved from [[Stadion am Bruchweg]] into their newly built [[Coface Arena]].<ref name="kickerSonderheft2011-12">{{cite journal|last=Smentek|first=Klaus|date=18 July 2011|title=kicker Bundesliga Sonderheft 2011/12|journal=[[Kicker (sports magazine)|Kicker]]|location=Nuremberg|issn=0948-7964|language=de|display-authors=etal}}</ref> Other changes included the completion of works at [[MHPArena|Mercedes-Benz Arena]], which was converted to a football-only stadium during the 2009–10 and 2010–11 seasons, and the renaming of [[Impuls Arena]], the ground of promoted team [[FC Augsburg]], to ''SGL Arena'' effective from the beginning of the season after [[SGL Carbon]] acquired the naming rights for the structure in May 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=impuls arena wird zur SGL Arena|url=http://www.fcaugsburg.de/cms/website.php?sid=0be85c25bd9970418e299bb446aa9b6f&id=/index/aktuell/news/data16645.htm|work=Official website|publisher=[[FC Augsburg]]|access-date=18 May 2011|language=de|archive-date=22 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422193743/http://www.fcaugsburg.de/cms/website.php?sid=0be85c25bd9970418e299bb446aa9b6f&id=%2Findex%2Faktuell%2Fnews%2Fdata16645.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Promotion/relegation play-offs==
[[Hertha BSC]] as 16th-placed team faced third-placed [[2011–12 2. Bundesliga]] side [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] in a two-legged play-off. Fortuna Düsseldorf won 4–3 on aggregate and thus were promoted for the [[2012–13 Bundesliga]] season while Hertha BSC were relegated to the [[2012–13 2. Bundesliga]].

Following the second leg, which was marred by several incidents of crowd disturbances, Hertha appealed the result.<ref name="HerthaAppeal">{{cite news|title=Hertha to appeal defeat after play-off drama|url=http://asia.eurosport.com/football/bundesliga/2011-2012/hertha-to-appeal-defeat_sto3273587/story.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141103113309/http://asia.eurosport.com/football/bundesliga/2011-2012/hertha-to-appeal-defeat_sto3273587/story.shtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 November 2014|access-date=16 May 2012|newspaper=[[Eurosport]]|date=16 May 2012}}</ref> On 21 May the [[DFB Sports Court]] rejected this appeal, having considered that these crowd disturbances did not psychologically impinge the Hertha players and that the referee's handling of the situation was sound. However, Hertha appealed again, this time to the Federal Court of the German FA.<ref>{{cite news|title=Einspruch abgewiesen: Doch Hertha geht vors Bundesgericht|url=https://www.kicker.de/einspruch-abgewiesen_doch-hertha-geht-vors-bundesgericht-569331/artikel|access-date=21 May 2012|magazine=[[Kicker (sports magazine)|Kicker]]|location=Germany|date=21 May 2012|language=de}}</ref> On 25 May, the Federal Court of the German FA also rejected the appeal.<ref name="Hertha2ndAppeal">{{cite news|title=Hertha play-off appeal rejected|url=http://www.bundesliga.de/en/liga/news/2011/0000213303.php|access-date=25 May 2012|publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga|DFL]]|date=25 May 2012|archive-date=17 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120617035429/http://www.bundesliga.de/en/liga/news/2011/0000213303.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 19 June, Hertha BSC decided not to appeal the decision, marking their immediate return to the 2. Bundesliga.<ref name="HerthaRelegation">{{cite news|title=Hertha's relegation set in stone|url=http://www.bundesliga.de/en/liga/news/2011/0000215004.php|access-date=19 June 2012|publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga|DFL]]|date=19 June 2012|archive-date=24 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120624001359/http://www.bundesliga.de/en/liga/news/2011/0000215004.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>
